chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazzaz informed me. He said: Musa b. Isma'il narrated to me from his father from Musa b. Ja'far from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).

He said: A Jew had lent the Messenger of Allah gold coins, and he came to collect. He said to him: O Jew, I do not have anything to give you. He said: I will not leave you, Muhammad, until you repay me. He said: Then I shall sit with you. He sat with him until he prayed Thuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and the morning prayer in that spot. The companions were threatening the Jew. The Messenger of Allah looked at them and said: What are you doing to him? They said: O Messenger of Allah, a Jew has confined you! He said: My Lord did not send me to oppress a treaty-holder or anyone else. When daytime came, the Jew said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. Half my wealth is in the way of Allah. By Allah, I only did what I did to see your description in the Torah. I read your description in the Torah: Muhammad son of Abdullah, born in Mecca, emigrating to Tayba, neither rude nor harsh nor boisterous, not adorning himself with vulgarity or profane speech. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah. Here is my wealth -- judge in it as Allah has revealed. And the Jew had great wealth.

key_terms.بِفَظٍّ وَلَا غَلِيظٍ: neither rude nor harsh -- the Torah's description of the Prophet's character
key_terms.دَنَانِيرُ: gold coins (dinars) -- the debt owed by the Prophet
key_terms.مُعَاهَدًا: a treaty-holder -- a non-Muslim with a covenant of protection
key_terms.نَعْتِكَ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ: your description in the Torah -- the Jewish man's verification of prophecy

ai.seo_question: How did a Jewish man test the Prophet Muhammad's character according to his description in the Torah?
ai.summary: Imam Ali narrates that a Jewish man to whom the Prophet owed gold coins came to collect the debt. When the Prophet said he had nothing to give, the Jew refused to leave until paid. Rather than dismissing the creditor, the Prophet sat with him through five prayers. When the companions threatened the Jew, the Prophet rebuked them, saying 'My Lord did not send me to oppress a treaty-holder or anyone else.' Moved by this display of character, the Jew declared his faith in Islam, donated half his wealth, and revealed he had been testing the Prophet against his description in the Torah: born in Mecca, emigrating to Tayba, neither rude nor harsh nor boisterous, not adorning himself with vulgarity or profane speech. This account demonstrates how the Prophet's moral conduct itself served as evidence of his prophethood.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazzaz informed us. He said: Musa b. Isma`il narrated to me from his father from Musa b. Ja`far from his father from his forefathers (as) from Amir al-Mu’minin (as).

He said: A Jew had lent the Messenger of Allah (s) gold coins, and he came to collect the debt. So, he said to him: O Jew! I do not have anything to give you. He said: I will not leave you, Muhammad, until I collect the debt from you. So, he (s) said: Allow me to sit with you. So, he (s) sat with him until he prayed Thuhr, `Asr, Maghrib, the final `Isha’, and the morning prayer in that spot. The companions of the Messenger of Allah were threatening him and making promises to him. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) looked at them and said: What are you doing with him? So, they said: O Messenger of Allah! A Jew has confined you! So, he (s) said: My Lord did not send me to persecute a person of a treaty or others. So, when daytime came, the Jew said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and I bear witness that Muhammad is His Servant and His Messenger. I give half my wealth in the way of Allah. Surely, by Allah, I did not do what I did to you except so that I may see your description in the Torah, for surely, I read in your description in the Torah: “Muhammad, the son of `Abdullah. He is born in Mecca, and he will flee to Tayba. He is neither rude, nor difficult, nor boisterous. He does not adorn himself with revilement nor with profane speech.” I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah. Here is my wealth, so do with it as Allah reveals regarding it – and he was a Jew with great wealth.
